source: name of the game: 'Floor is ALIVE'. basics of the game:The floor grows, shrinks, cracks, wiggles, and sprouts obstacles. The map feels like a living creature instead of a static arena. there is lava, (basically like floor is lava expect the floor is always moving) the rounds will last 2 minutes and your goal is to be the last on alive!

image_prompt.text: Pools and rivers of lava spread across the floor as the killing hazard
Raised sections of the living floor that swell up as temporary safe ground
Cracking, fracturing floor plates that break apart under the players
A floor built like the skin of a living creature - organic, fleshy, wrinkled, breathing rather than paved
Spiky organic growths and jagged obstacles sprouting up out of the floor

layout_placement.text: An enclosed round boundary holding all players inside the living arena for the round

notes: Preset Disaster Survival contributed terrain-tiered and destructible-cluster; the prompt only says the floor rises, shrinks, and cracks.
The defining feature - a floor that continuously deforms during the round - is not expressible as a layout option; the image can only draw one frame of it.
Win condition (last player alive, 2-minute rounds) has no field in the handoff.

open_questions.ask: How many players per round? That sets whether the arena is a 150-stud pit or a 400-stud field.
When the round timer ends with several players alive, does everyone win or does the floor sudden-death them?

theme: Organic / Living Creature - fleshy undulating ground shot through with glowing lava

coverage_missing.ask: How many players are in a round, and how big should the arena be?
What happens if more than one player survives the full 2 minutes?
Should the living floor read as cartoon-gross or genuinely horrific?

answers.ask: How many players per round? That sets whether the arena is a 150-stud pit or a 400-stud field.
answers.answer: Use 12 players per round, with a compact arena sized for fast, readable survival gameplay.

answers.ask: When the round timer ends with several players alive, does everyone win or does the floor sudden-death them?
answers.answer: Everyone still alive when the 2-minute timer ends wins the round; the goal is simply to survive the living floor.
